I stand firmly with Secretary Hegseth. Impeachment is one of the most serious powers entrusted to Congress, and Massie’s rush to bring these charges directly to the House floor treats that responsibility like a political stunt.

When the House pursued the impeachment of Mayorkas, the resolution went to committee, hearings were held, and articles were considered before the full House acted. Secretary Hegseth deserves the same process.

At a minimum, these charges should be referred to the House Judiciary Committee, where the evidence can be examined and the Secretary given a fair opportunity to respond. If Massie believes his case is strong, he should have no problem letting it withstand that scrutiny.

Skipping those steps is a disservice to Secretary Hegseth, the House, and the American people.

This bogus impeachment push is political theater.
